historyItems.originalTitle: Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX lose over $420 billion in combined market cap after midterms
historyItems.originalSummary: SpaceX and Tesla shares fell about 9% and 11%, respectively, on Thursday afternoon as investors worried that Elon Musk could face new congressional investigations and his companies could encounter stricter regulation after the US midterm elections.As if the election results were not enough, which saw the Republican Party, which Musk poured nearly half a billion into, being pummelled out of the US Congress, the turmoil at the bourse may just be the beginning of the world's richest man's chagrin.The declines, which coincided with a broader technology-sector sell-off, pushed combined market-cap losses for SpaceX and Tesla to more than $420 billion since Tuesday’s close.As per a CNBC report, by the close of trading on Thursday, SpaceX and Tesla had lost a combined approximately $456 billion in market capitalisation.According to Forbes, which keeps a reliable database of the richest in the world, Musk’s net worth, which exceeded $1 trillion after SpaceX’s initial public offering in June, has now fallen below $800 billion. He lost about $90 billion over the past week but remains the world’s richest person.Musk was the largest donor to Republican candidates and causes during the midterms, contributing more than $470 million, the Financial Times first reported.Despite his support for the GOP’s fundraising efforts, most of the candidates Musk backed lost their races.Democrats secured control of both the House and Senate. In Texas, home to both Tesla and SpaceX, Democratic Sen.-elect James Talarico and Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa defeated longtime Musk allies: state Attorney General Ken Paxton and Gov. Greg Abbott.Tesla and SpaceX are expanding their AI infrastructure in Texas and plan to build Terafab, a massive complex in Grimes County that will house both a data center and a sprawling semiconductor factory.According to company job postings, SpaceX also intends to develop a “supercomputer” at Starbase, its launch facility and company town in Texas.Deutsche Bank analysts, who spoke to CNBC, have warned that SpaceX’s computing expansion in Texas may face delays. They said the company could need to raise capital spending to comply with stricter regulations expected to govern data centre development.CNN first reported, citing an aide to a Democratic senator, that Musk and SpaceX had been instructed to retain records related to restrictions on a military version of Starlink in Ukraine. Those restrictions limited Ukraine’s ability to defend itself against Russian attacks.Regulatory scrutiny could also jeopardise Musk’s proposed merger of SpaceX and Tesla, an idea he has promoted while acknowledging that it would first require shareholder approval.Read Also: Hyundai cars can now cut your insurance premium by up to 15% if you drive safely

historyItems.originalTitle: US proposes space launch rule changes in potential boost for SpaceX
historyItems.originalSummary: The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) proposed changes to commercial space launch and re-entry rules. The move aims to reduce licensing delays and support a rapid rise in launch activity across the country.The proposals could particularly benefit Elon Musk’s SpaceX and Jeff Bezos’s Blue Origin. Both companies operate high-frequency launch programs and require repeated regulatory approvals for rockets, satellites and reusable vehicles..What the FAA Proposes.The FAA has put forward three key changes. First, operators would gain flexibility to switch off a rocket’s flight-termination system earlier in a mission and reactivate it later, provided they meet the agency’s safety conditions for that phase.Second, the regulator proposes clearer rules on when a launch must be aborted. The revised language would explain how companies should assess the risks of ending a flight early versus allowing it to continue after it can no longer achieve its objective.Third, the FAA wants to simplify how operators assess spacecraft breakup during uncontrolled re-entry. Companies could use existing debris analyses to show that fragments are unlikely to cause multiple casualties on the ground..A Boost for SpaceX.The changes would make launch approvals easier for SpaceX and Blue Origin, according to the FAA. SpaceX, which dominates US commercial launch activity, stands to gain the most since it conducts missions at a far higher cadence than its rivals.Faster approvals could help SpaceX expand Starlink satellite deployments, accelerate Starship development and reduce waiting periods between missions. Blue Origin could also benefit as it scales its New Glenn rocket program.The proposals follow earlier FAA moves to allow electronic launch applications, combine three safety analyses into one submission and give operators greater flexibility in demonstrating safe operations..Preparing for Higher Launch Volumes.The White House wants at least 1,000 commercial launches and re-entries annually by 2030. That target compares with 178 launches last year and marks a tenfold increase from 2013.To manage this growth, the FAA is expanding its Office of Commercial Space Transportation. It has named an associate administrator and is hiring aerospace engineers to speed up safety reviews and mission authorisations.The agency also plans a broader overhaul of its space-licensing framework beginning in 2027. The initiative signals a shift towards a more predictable and scalable regulatory system for the commercial space economy.Also Read: Qualcomm to Supply 5G Technology for SpaceX's Nationwide Network.Join our WhatsApp Channel to get the latest news, exclusives and videos on WhatsApp

historyItems.originalTitle: Skyworks Stock Sinks as Android Woes Delay the Qorvo’s Merger Payoff
historyItems.originalSummary: IRVINE, Calif., Nov. 03, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Skyworks Solutions, Inc. (Nasdaq: SWKS), a global leader in high-performance RF, precision timing, power management and mixed-signal solutions, today reported fourth fiscal quarter and fiscal year 2026 results for the period ended Oct. 2, 2026. Skyworks’ revenue for its fourth fiscal quarter of 2026 was $1,046 million. Skyworks’ GAAP diluted earnings per share were $0.15 and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share were $1.28. For fiscal year 2026, Skyworks’ revenue was $3.96 billion, with GAAP diluted earnings per share of $1.14 and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $5.05. “Today marks a new chapter for Skyworks,” said Phil Brace, chief executive officer and president of Skyworks. “Combining with Qorvo gives us the scale and the technology breadth to lead the next era of wireless, as AI moves from the infrastructure to the devices, vehicles and machines around us. In Smartphone, our portfolio now spans the RF front-end, from power management to the antenna, as 5G-Advanced and 6G drive a new cycle of RF complexity. In Diversified Growth Markets, our complementary RF GaN, power, and timing solutions expand our reach across Physical AI and Connected Edge, Defense and Aerospace, Infrastructure, and Automotive. Our focus now is execution: delivering for our customers, achieving $500 million or more of annual cost synergies and building a stronger, more diversified Skyworks.” Basis of Presentation and New Revenue Categories “Because our combination with Qorvo closed after the end of our fiscal fourth quarter, our reported September-quarter results are Skyworks standalone,” said Philip Carter, chief financial officer and senior vice president of Skyworks. “Combined September-quarter revenue of approximately $1.98 billion, which includes an additional week in Qorvo’s fiscal quarter, provides the starting point for our first quarter as a combined company. Beginning with our first fiscal quarter of 2027, we will report on a fully combined basis, with Smartphone and Diversified Growth Markets as our revenue categories.”

historyItems.originalTitle: Shares of Elon Musk’s Tesla and SpaceX Tumble After Republican Losses
historyItems.originalSummary: Thank you for your patience while we verify access. Elon Musk spent nearly $500 million supporting Republican candidates in the midterm elections, especially in his home state, Texas. After Democrats won sweeping victories, gaining control of both houses of Congress and capturing other important state races, shares of SpaceX and Tesla, which are both run by Mr. Musk, fell sharply on Wednesday. Tesla’s stock dropped when markets opened, and closed down more than 3 percent. SpaceX, which conducted a blockbuster public offering in June, followed a similar pattern, and was nearly 4 percent lower by the end of trading. The declines stood out among tech stocks, as Meta, Microsoft, Google and the wider stock market rallied at the start of trading. SpaceX and Tesla are exploring a merger , which could be complicated by a Congress controlled by Democrats, some of whom have already signaled their intent to investigate the world’s richest person and his companies. In recent years, Mr. Musk has antagonized Democrats, spending heavily to elect President Trump, involving himself deeply in firing federal workers and shutting down government agencies while aligning his companies’ interests with those of the administration. “They are going to need to plant new forests for all of the subpoenas we’ll be printing,” Senator Edward J. Markey, Democrat of Massachusetts, posted on X on Tuesday night about potential hearings for technology executives.

historyItems.title: 民主黨橫掃中期選舉後，馬斯克 (Elon Musk) 旗下 SpaceX 和特斯拉的股價在盤前下跌
historyItems.summary: As Democrats swept the 2026 midterm elections on Tuesday, November 3, shares of Elon Musk 's companies SpaceX and Tesla tumbled the following morning. The New York Times reported on Wednesday, November 4, that when markets opened, Tesla's stock fell more than 5 percent, and SpaceX fell more than 7 percent before recovering some of those losses. The world's richest man, 55, poured at least $474 million into the midterms in an attempt to keep Republicans in power, spending more money than any donor in a U.S. election cycle, not counting candidates who have funded their own runs for office, according to the outlet.

historyItems.originalTitle: Cresta Fills An Important Gap In Salesforce’s Customer Service AI Story
historyItems.originalSummary: Salesforce has signed a definitive agreement to buy Cresta, whose voice agents handle complex customer calls from start to finish, Salesforce said on Monday. The deal should close in the first quarter of Salesforce’s fiscal year 2028, subject to regulatory approvals. Salesforce did not disclose a price. It agreed to pay $2.7bn, according to a person familiar with the deal, as Valida Pau and Kevin McLaughlin reported for The Information . TNW has not independently verified the figure. Cresta is nine years old and started out at Stanford University’s AI Lab, The Information reported. The deal builds up Salesforce’s customer service business, the outlet wrote. Cresta calls itself a voice-first operating system for customer experience. Its voice agents hold natural, real-time conversations and handle interruptions, Salesforce said. Marriott, Comcast and Alaska Airlines use them at enterprise scale. The same platform guides human representatives during live calls and analyses every interaction. It also coaches staff and tests the voice agents, holding both to the same quality standard. “Voice is where service is hardest to get right, and where it matters most to customers,” said Kishan Chetan, EVP and GM of Agentforce and Service Cloud at Salesforce. Salesforce plans to join Cresta with Service Cloud, its customer service software. The aim is to link each conversation to the customer’s history and to the outcome, which Salesforce lists as resolution, retention and revenue. After the deal closes, Cresta will keep supporting the contact centre and telephony platforms its customers use today, Salesforce said. “Now, by uniting our platform with Salesforce, we will realize our full vision at scale, embedding real-time conversation intelligence and agentic experiences directly into Salesforce’s first-class customer service Platform,” said Ping Wu, chief executive of Cresta. Cresta follows other recent Salesforce deals. It agreed a $5.7bn Braze deal on 20 October. Days before Cresta, it announced plans to buy Rune , a national security software company.

historyItems.originalTitle: Aehr Test Systems: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
historyItems.originalSummary: On its first quarter of fiscal 2027 earnings call, held on Nov. 2, 2026, Aehr Test Systems ( AEHR +5.59% ) raised its full-year revenue outlook to $150 million after sales tripled year over year. The semiconductor test equipment manufacturer is capitalizing on rapid capacity expansion across artificial intelligence (AI) processors and optical interconnects. Expanding production requirements across multiple customer accounts provide meaningful operating leverage as shipment volumes scale. Three key takeaways from management explain how this growth trajectory affects long-term value. Aehr Test spent years dependent on a narrow group of customers for the bulk of its revenue. Management has expanded its active pipeline across more than 12 customers in AI processors, silicon photonics, silicon carbide, and gallium nitride, creating a broader base for multiyear revenue growth. Order activity drove effective backlog, which includes confirmed customer orders awaiting shipment, to $109 million as of Nov. 1. That order volume gives management strong revenue visibility and allows it to scale asset-light manufacturing capacity through third-party factory partners in Southeast Asia without heavy capital expenditures. A major AI accelerator supplier completed a benchmark evaluation and ordered a full test cell for evaluation at an outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) partner in Taiwan. Testing multi-chip processor packages before final assembly prevents costly chip failures, positioning Aehr Test for high-volume production orders across multiple product lines. Demand for AI processors is accelerating rapidly, and execution is matching pace. Aehr Test maintains a proprietary technology position in full-wafer contactors and multi-zone thermal control. Management is watching customer qualification timelines and contract manufacturing capacity expansion. Converting ongoing benchmark evaluations into high-volume production orders forms the foundation for long-term expansion.

historyItems.originalTitle: Aehr Revenue Triples as AI Orders Pile Up: Rapid Earnings Reaction
historyItems.originalSummary: Interested in Aehr Test Systems? Here are five stocks we like better. Aehr Test Systems reported a record fiscal Q1: Revenue rose 200% year over year to $33.0 million, while non-GAAP net income reached $9.4 million. Bookings more than quadrupled to $46.7 million, lifting backlog to $100.9 million. The company raised its fiscal 2027 outlook to $150 million in revenue, which would represent approximately 200% annual growth, while maintaining its expectation for non-GAAP net income of at least 20% of revenue. AI semiconductor demand is driving expansion: Aehr is adding wafer-level and package-level burn-in capacity for hyperscale and AI-chip customers, expanding manufacturing operations in Southeast Asia and Taiwan, and expects consumables to contribute about 35% of fiscal-year revenue.

historyItems.originalTitle: Valuation Compression Pulls Down KLA (KLAC) Despite Raised Outlook
historyItems.originalSummary: Bristol Gate Capital Partners , an investment management company, published its Q3 2026 investor letter for the "US Equity Strategy". The letter can be downloaded here . The US Equity Strategy lagged the S&P 500 (+2.3%) in Q3 2026, as declines in industrial and semiconductor-equipment holdings weighed against gains in tech. Despite this relative drag, the strategy continued to outpace the index in terms of dividend growth. Portfolio fundamentals were solid in the quarter, with 21 out of 22 holdings exceeding earnings forecasts, six raising guidance, and several boosting dividends. Key contributors included Microsoft, Cintas, and McKesson, while KLA, Applied Materials, and GE Aerospace negatively impacted performance. Bristol Gate's portfolio remains positioned for long-term compounding via robust balance sheets and cash-flow-funded dividend growth, providing resilience against high interest rates, top-heavy market concentration, and AI credit friction. Also, check the Fund's top five holdings to see its best picks for 2026.

historyItems.originalTitle: Here’s What a $10,000 Investment in TSMC Stock Will Be Worth by 2030
historyItems.originalSummary: When you hear investors talk about AI, names like Nvidia ( NVDA +3.50% ) and AMD ( AMD +11.03% ) pop up all the time. While those are great stock picks, investors can also go a layer deeper and look at a stock like Taiwan Semiconductor ( TSM +6.28% ) . Taiwan Semiconductor is a chip foundry, which means that it manufactures the chips that giants like Nvidia and AMD design. Because it's selling its services to most of the competitors in the AI chip race, TSMC is set to keep profiting from the infrastructure build-out no matter which of them is gaining or losing ground. All TSMC cares about is whether companies are spending more and more on data centers each year. If they are, then TSMC will need to produce more chips to meet demand. Considering the language the market has heard from some of the AI hyperscalers and computing unit providers recently, I'd say it's a safe bet that 2027 will be another year for the record books. That bodes well for TSMC, and I think a $5,000 investment made now could be worth far more by 2030.

historyItems.originalTitle: Intel tops Q3 earnings estimates, but falls short of Q4 outlook on sluggish PC sales as stock plunges 20%
historyItems.originalSummary: Intel Corporation INTC reported solid third-quarter 2026 results, with adjusted earnings and revenues beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate. Strong demand for server processors, driven by artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure investments, supported top-line growth despite weakness in the PC market. Non-GAAP earnings surged 126.1% year over year to 52 cents per share, surpassing the consensus estimate of 39 cents by 33.33%. Revenues increased 20.9% to $16.51 billion, beating the consensus estimate of $16.44 billion by 0.44%. Data Center and AI revenues jumped 78% year over year, reflecting strong demand across hyperscale, enterprise and neo-cloud customers. However, a soft fourth-quarter outlook overshadowed the feel-good factor for investors and shares plunged more than 25% in pre-market trading.

historyItems.title: SpaceX 供應商意法半導體預測人工智慧和衛星將帶來強勁銷售
historyItems.summary: By Mauro Orru STMicroelectronics projected robust sales growth for the year as the build-out of data centers to power artificial-intelligence models and the deployment of satellites to provide connectivity services fuel demand for semiconductors. The European chip maker, which counts Apple and Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX among its clients, said 2026 revenue should grow nearly 23% on year to roughly $14.5 billion. Meanwhile, its gross margin--a closely watched measure of pricing power--should increase to about 36.4% from 33.9% last year. The company had refrained from providing detailed annual guidance until now , as it embarks on the final quarter, gaining better visibility into what is driving demand.

The company had refrained from providing detailed annual guidance until now , as it embarks on the final quarter, gaining better visibility into what is driving demand. It expects sales of about $4.15 billion this quarter compared with $3.33 billion a year earlier, above a Visible Alpha forecast of nearly $4.12 billion. Its annual sales projection is also above a Visible Alpha forecast of $14.41 billion. Chief Executive Jean-Marc Chery singled out data centers and satellites as key drivers for growth this year. Like other chip makers, STMicroelectronics is reaping the benefits of hundreds of billions of dollars in spending commitments from some of the world's largest tech groups to build out AI infrastructure. STMicroelectronics stock has nearly doubled in value since the year began, riding a wave of investor fervor around AI that lifted global semiconductor stocks. In a sign of how fast demand for chips to power energy-intensive data centers is building up, STMicroelectronics in July projected revenue from data centers above $1 billion in 2026 and well above $2 billion in 2027 compared with prior guidance of about $1 billion and roughly $2 billion, respectively. That marked the second time the company raised its AI forecasts this year. Alongside data centers, space also provides a key revenue stream for STMicroelectronics and other chip makers that supply semiconductors for low-Earth-orbit satellite constellations. The company expects well above $3 billion in revenue between 2026 and 2028 for the supply of equipment to be used in space, a forecast that for now excludes potential benefits from orbital data centers. Low Earth-orbit satellite networks are closer to Earth than traditional constellations, making them ideal to beam low-latency broadband directly to smartphones in parts of the world where cell towers are unavailable. SpaceX's Starlink provides direct-to-device connectivity to users in several countries, including Ukraine, where damage to terrestrial networks because of the war is common. STMicroelectronics had long relied on the automotive industry to generate a significant portion of its sales. Data centers and satellites have allowed the group to diversify its revenue streams and become less tied to carmakers. The auto industry in recent years had slowly been digesting chip inventories it built at the height of the pandemic, weighing on demand for new orders in a blow to STMicroelectronics. historyItems.originalTitle: AI Data Center Supplier Amphenol Jumps On Earnings Beat
historyItems.originalSummary: Burke Wealth Management, an investment management company, released its "Focused Growth Strategy" Q3 2026 investor letter. A copy of the letter can be downloaded here . The fund delivered strong results in the third quarter of 2026, benefiting from a sharp recovery in enterprise software and solid corporate earnings amid continued market volatility. The composite returned 10.8% net of fees, substantially outperforming the S&P 500 Total Return Index's 2.3% gain, while its year-to-date return reached 20.0%, compared with 12.7% for the benchmark. The firm attributed the quarter's strength partly to investors reassessing the long-term value of enterprise software platforms that can securely connect AI models with proprietary business data. Burke believes these platforms can serve as essential AI "harnesses," providing permissions, security, and context for enterprise applications, although it cautions that AI agents could challenge traditional software business models and seat-based pricing. Looking ahead, Burke remains optimistic about the remainder of 2026, citing strong corporate earnings growth and the transition from AI infrastructure investment toward practical applications that may improve productivity and consumer experiences. In addition, please check the Fund's top five holdings to know its best picks in 2026.

Special Report : See How You Could Qualify for the Fastest Second Citizenship as an American Today (From International Living) GE Vernova (NYSE: GEV) gave investors plenty to like in its third-quarter report , released before the open on Wednesday, Oct. 28. Revenue climbed 27% to $12.6 billion, comfortably ahead of the roughly $12 billion analysts expected, and earnings of $4.81 per share beat the $4.03 consensus. Orders nearly doubled on an organic basis to $29.3 billion, while total backlog grew by $20 billion in a single quarter to $197 billion. Management also raised its 2026 outlook for revenue, margins, and free cash flow, and doubled its share repurchase authorization to $20 billion. Still, the stock slid as much as 6.6% intraday before closing down about 2% for the day, leaving it 27% below its 52-week high. That reaction says a lot. With AI infrastructure stocks under pressure, a bigger backlog alone no longer impresses the market. The more important question is what that backlog is actually made of, and how much of it is turning into firm business. Larry Benedict, who ran a $900 million hedge fund and posted 20 consecutive years without a loss, including over $274 million in audited net income between 2004 and 2012, says one long forgotten American company already holds what Musk needs. Firm backlog consists of signed equipment orders. Slot reservation agreements hold a customer’s place in the production line, but they aren’t orders yet. As of June 30, the company had 53 GW of firm backlog and 63 GW of slot reservations. In the third quarter, it converted 13 GW of reservations into firm orders, up from 10 GW the prior quarter, while shipping 5 GW of equipment. That pushed firm backlog up to 64 GW and brought reservations down to 58 GW, for 122 GW under contract in total. Notably, that’s the shift management pointed to last quarter , with firm orders now outweighing reservations. The company also raised its year-end goal to at least 130 GW under contract, up from 125 GW. Production Is Keeping Pace Of course, converting reservations only matters if GE Vernova can actually build the turbines. The company planned to reach 20 GW of annual gas turbine output in the third quarter, and shipping 5 GW that quarter is consistent with that pace. historyItems.originalSummary: Fred Alger Management , an investment management company, released its "Alger Spectra Fund" third-quarter 2026 investor letter. The letter can be downloaded here . During the third quarter of 2026, U.S. equities delivered modest gains, with the S&P 500 advancing 2%. Despite robust corporate earnings and resilient consumer spending, market breadth remained weak as 60% of S&P 500 constituents closed lower. Against this backdrop, the fund lagged the Russell 3000 Growth Index. Class A shares of the fund returned 0.29% without a sales charge and -4.98% with sales charges, compared to 0.45% for the index. Consumer Discretionary and Tech drove the relative performance, whereas Communication Services and Utilities dragged. Macro headwinds weighed on sectors like Energy following oil supply disruptions. On the short side, a position in an IT consulting firm detracted from returns, while a short in an advertising technology company generated positive gains following its weak earnings report and rising competitive threats. Amid these shifting dynamics, the fund continues to prioritize disciplined stock selection to capture long-term opportunities across the expanding AI ecosystem. In addition, please check the Fund's top five holdings to know its best picks in 2026.

historyItems.originalTitle: GE Vernova stock gains on earnings beat, raised guidance
historyItems.originalSummary: Shares of GE Vernova T&D India Ltd. gain nearly 5% on Monday, November 2, after the company reported better-than-expected earnings in the second quarter.Strong execution led to its revenue growth of 32% year-on-year during the September quarter. Better execution also aided its profitability. The company's EBITDA margin expansion was primarily led by gross margin expansion and operating leverage.The company's profit after tax increased 44.15% to ₹431 crore from ₹299 crore last year. It was also 11.7% higher than the CNBC-TV18 poll of ₹385.7 crore.Revenue for the quarter stood at ₹2,027 crore, also marginally higher than the CNBC-TV18 poll of ₹1,970 croreEarnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization increased 38.8% to ₹549.7 crore from ₹396 crore. A CNBC-TV18 poll had projected the figure to be ₹501 crore.Its EBITDA margin expanded to 27.1% from 25.7% in the year-ago period, higher than the 25.4% poll expectation.GE Vernova T&D's order inflow during the quarter stood at ₹2,440 crore compared to ₹1,140 crore in the previous year and ₹1,601 crore in the same quarter last year. This took the company's order backlog to ₹21,440 crore, compared to ₹20,930 crore earlier.The company's management, in its post-earnings conference call, said it has maintained its FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of mid-20s. It also expects over 30% annual execution growth over the next three to four years on the back of the strong backlog and the Barmer HVDC order.The management expects to book Power Grid's Barmer HVDC project in the third quarter of this fiscal.It has also maintained its base order inflow target of ₹7,200 crore to ₹8,000 crore for FY27. It expects STATCOM and data centre orders to pick up from the fourth quarter.The management said FY28 will see bidding for 2-3 HVDC projects. It also expects revenue contribution from existing HDFC projects to commence mainly from financial year 2028 and 2029.As a result, Motilal Oswal has marginally raised its estimates by 7% and 1% respectively for financial year 2027 and 2028, to factor in the performance of the first half.NomuraNomura has a "buy" recommendation and target price of ₹6,090 per share on the stock. historyItems.originalTitle: Amazon cloud capacity largely sold out through 2027, CEO Jassy says
historyItems.originalSummary: AWS has largely booked its computing capacity for major customer commitments in 2027, with some commitments extending into 2028, according to Amazon CEO Andy Jassy. Speaking on the a16z Show podcast on October 23, Jassy said AWS was struggling to meet demand from AI developers and enterprise customers despite Amazon’s plans to spend approximately $220 billion on capital expenditure in 2026. “2027 is largely sold out,” Jassy said, adding that “a good chunk of 2028 is sold out.” The company’s capacity for 2026 has also been fully committed, excluding resources reserved for on-demand services. Jassy clarified that the commitments primarily concern large allocations of computing capacity rather than all AWS services. The company continues to reserve resources for on-demand workloads through Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) and its managed generative AI service, Amazon Bedrock. Amazon has not disclosed the exact amount of computing capacity committed for 2027 and 2028 or how much remains available for on-demand customers. Jassy identified data centre availability, electricity, and memory supply as constraints on AWS’s ability to expand computing capacity. He said shortages affecting different infrastructure components would continue beyond 2027. Memory shortages are also affecting how AWS allocates resources between AI and conventional cloud workloads. AI accelerators use high-bandwidth memory (HBM), while conventional servers typically rely on other forms of dynamic random-access memory (DRAM). Jassy said AWS faces allocation decisions as demand for both AI and non-AI computing services increases. During Amazon’s second-quarter 2026 earnings call, Jassy said data centre spending typically begins about two years before servers can be put into service. Servers and networking equipment are generally purchased only a few months before they are needed. This allows AWS to reduce equipment purchases if customer demand falls short of expectations. Its data centre infrastructure, meanwhile, is designed to remain operational for more than 30 years.

historyItems.title: 安全金鑰加強受保護的軍事衛星通信
historyItems.summary: At any given moment, a U.S. Air Force pilot may be maneuvering an aircraft mid-mission, a U.S. Navy officer resurfacing a submarine after weeks undersea, or a U.S. Army technician offloading drone data in a combat zone.
historyItems.originalTitle: Secure keys strengthen protected military satellite communications
historyItems.originalSummary: At any given moment, a U.S. Air Force pilot may be maneuvering an aircraft mid-mission, a U.S. Navy officer resurfacing a submarine after weeks undersea, or a U.S. Army technician offloading drone data in a combat zone. Each operation depends on satellite communications (satcom) and, specifically, on cryptographic keys that allow terminals to communicate securely while keeping adversaries locked out. At the scale of modern operations, managing these keys is a technical challenge. Every terminal needs to have the right keys at the right time, quickly and securely, and if any keys are compromised, they need to be refreshed without leaving out devices that may be offline, disconnected, or under attack. MIT Lincoln Laboratory researchers have now solved this challenge with the Protected Anti-Jam Tactical Satcom (PATS) Key Management System (KMS) Prototype. This new architecture enables keys to refresh rapidly across terminals dispersed worldwide, even in contested or bandwidth-constrained environments. "We're enabling the nation to achieve highly assured, highly available communications. Even when adversaries know where forces are operating and are trying to stop them from communicating, they're unable to do so, because we've built in smarts across this entire system to keep talking," says Joseph Sobchuk, a principal investigator of the PATS KMS Prototype program and researcher in the Secure Resilient Systems and Technology Group . This architecture is being adopted as the cryptographic backbone of the U.S. Space Force's next-generation satcom system, PATS. The KMS Prototype serves as the gold-standard reference implementation for the industry-built operational KMS, which will be integrated across the PATS ecosystem, encompassing satellites, user terminals on military platforms, and ground-based communication hubs. Developed under sponsorship of the Space Force's Space Systems Command (SSC), the KMS Prototype reflects Lincoln Laboratory's end-to-end approach to technology development, from shaping the core key-management concepts to putting them into practice in a prototype to transitioning a technical baseline to government and industry. For this transitioned innovation, the SSC and Lincoln Laboratory team received a 2025 R&D 100 Award , recognizing the KMS Prototype among the year's most impactful new technologies. Cryptographic keys are foundational to secure communications. These keys, strings of random characters used by cryptographic algorithms, help protect communications by encrypting data and supporting protected transmission patterns, such as frequency hopping . Without key protection, the communications sent and received by terminals are more susceptible to eavesdropping and interference. Historically, operators manually uploaded keys to terminals before missions. More recently, some systems have supported over-the-air key updates, but bandwidth constraints, security concerns, and operational complexity have limited real-time, wide-scale refresh. historyItems.originalTitle: Google and Oracle are partnering to bring Google TPUs to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure
historyItems.originalSummary: OCI will be the first hyperscaler outside Google to offer Google TPUsLAS VEGAS, Oct. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Oracle AI World -- Oracle and Google today announced that Google's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) will be available through Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), marking the first time Google TPUs will be offered on a hyperscale cloud platform outside Google. By bringing Google's purpose-built TPUs to OCI's AI compute portfolio, customers gain the flexibility to match their most demanding workloads with infrastructure designed for near-linear scalability and highly optimized economics. "Different AI workloads have different compute needs," said Mahesh Thiagarajan, president, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, Oracle. "Bringing Google TPUs to OCI gives customers access to multiple leading AI compute architectures in one cloud. That choice gives them the flexibility to choose the right infrastructure for the performance, throughput, and economics of each AI workload."Google TPUs are custom accelerators co-designed with open software to power the entire AI lifecycle—from frontier training and large-scale inference to the multi-step reasoning data demands of agentic AI. OCI will provide the power, cooling, and datacenter networking to deploy Google TPUs at scale within its infrastructure."The next generation of AI will require a diverse range of compute," said Amin Vahdat, senior vice president and chief technologist, AI & Infrastructure, Google. "TPUs give customers a powerful, purpose-built option for demanding training and inference workloads. Bringing Google TPUs to OCI will give more organizations access to this technology and greater flexibility in how they build and run their most complex AI applications."More AI Compute Options for Every WorkloadAs models grow and production inference demands increase, the performance and economics of every training run and inference request become increasingly important. Google's TPU architecture is designed to maximize AI processing from each watt of electricity, with fast access to model data and rapid communication between chips.Google TPUs can support large-model training and post-training, including dense and mixture-of-experts models (MoE), as well as production inference for reasoning, agentic, and long-context applications. Customers will be able to choose Google TPUs within OCI, optimized for their workloads, performance requirements, and cost objectives.Drawing on more than a decade of custom AI silicon development, Google's TPU portfolio delivers purpose-built compute optimized for massive machine learning workloads. Google's eighth-generation TPU introduces two purpose-built architectures: TPU 8t for training and TPU 8i for inference. TPU 8t cuts frontier model development cycles from months to weeks, delivering nearly 3x the compute performance per pod over the previous generation, while TPU 8i is designed to handle the iterative work of many specialized agents.Google TPUs on OCI will be available in calendar year 2027, ramping over a multi-year period to meet customer needs.Additional ResourcesLearn more about Oracle C

historyItems.originalTitle: OpenAI expands partnership with Oracle to bring its apps to ChatGPT
historyItems.originalSummary: OpenAI said it is expanding its partnership with Oracle to bring business applications and AI agents into ChatGPT, while also helping power new Oracle offerings, according to an OpenAI announcement published on Oct. 27, 2026. The update extends a relationship that has already moved beyond infrastructure and into enterprise distribution. In its announcement, OpenAI said the companies are working to place Oracle business applications and AI agents inside ChatGPT, and to support new Oracle products through the collaboration. The statement did not include pricing, rollout timing, customer counts or a product launch schedule. The partnership has been building through multiple prior steps. OpenAI said on Aug. 7, 2026 that eligible Oracle Universal Credits can be used to purchase OpenAI API models, Codex and ChatGPT Work through Oracle Marketplace. Oracle also said on Oct. 16, 2026 that its own employees were adopting Enterprise ChatGPT as part of its AI-transformation update, indicating internal use of OpenAI software within the company. The expansion comes against a broader backdrop of joint infrastructure development. Oracle said in a June 11, 2024 announcement with Microsoft and OpenAI that Oracle Cloud Infrastructure would supply additional capacity by extending Microsoft’s Azure AI platform. OpenAI later named Oracle among the initial equity funders in its Jan. 21, 2025 Stargate announcement, which outlined an intention to invest $500 billion in U.S. AI infrastructure over four years. OpenAI then said on July 22, 2025 that it had agreed with Oracle to develop an additional 4.5 gigawatts of U.S. Stargate capacity, taking the total described in that update to more than 5 gigawatts under development and more than 2 million chips. Those figures described planned development, not already completed capacity. Oracle’s current infrastructure page, as of September 2026, said Abilene had delivered 75% of total capacity, while customer delivery at Shackelford and Doña Ana County was scheduled to begin in the first half of 2027. That timeline gives the partnership a physical infrastructure layer, while the new OpenAI announcement points to a broader software and distribution tie-up. There were no verified details in the source material on financial terms, revenue impact, exclusivity, or an official launch date for the new ChatGPT integrations. The timing of any further product rollout remains unknown from the supplied material.

historyItems.originalTitle: Nvidia, AMD to invest $4 billion in Meta as tech giants deepen AI partnership
historyItems.originalSummary: Meta Platforms Inc. today announced that Nvidia Corp. and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. plan to buy $4 billion worth of its shares. The chipmakers will purchase the equity as part of an up to $95 billion stock sale that the Facebook parent intends to kick off in the near future. The fundraising initiative will also include the participation of Broadcom Inc. Meta didn’t specify how much the company is investing, but it stated on Monday that Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom together plan to invest $5 billion. That suggests the networking chip giant will buy $1 billion in shares. Nvidia is investing $3 billion as part of a newly expanded partnership that also includes other components. Notably, Meta plans to broaden its use of the chipmaker’s Rubin graphics processing units and Vera central processing units. Companies often deploy the two chips together in Nvidia-designed DGX Vera Rubin NVL72 appliances. Each system includes 72 GPUs and 36 CPUs. Meta also plans to buy more Nvidia networking gear. It will expand its use of the Spectrum-X Ethernet product family, which includes SuperNICs and switches. SuperNICs are chips that connect servers to a data center’s network, while switches coordinate how traffic flows through that network. GPU clusters’ traffic patterns tend to change rapidly. As a result, connectivity bottlenecks sometimes emerge faster than the network can respond to them. Nvidia says that its Spectrum-X Ethernet product series addresses the challenge by checking GPU traffic for anomalies at sub-microsecond time intervals. A microsecond corresponds to one millionth of a second. Another focus of Meta’s planned network investment is Nvidia’s BlueField-4 chip family. The accelerators in the series are designed to speed common networking, storage and cybersecurity tasks. Nvidia will help Meta improve the performance and cost efficiency of its Muse large language model family. The effort will extend to the Facebook parent’s eponymous consumer AI agent. Additionally, Meta plans to explore “collaboration opportunities” related to Nvidia’s recently introduced OpenShell Reference Architecture. It’s a collection of technical resources that makes it easier to run the chipmaker’s OpenShell toolkit. The toolkit runs AI agents in isolated sandboxes designed to mitigate cybersecurity risks. “Nvidia and Meta are expanding our partnership to optimize the computing infrastructure end to end for capable, efficient and secure AI agents, so Muse can empower billions of people to achieve more and pursue greater ambitions,” said Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang. AMD, which will invest $1 billion in Meta, today revealed that the Facebook parent has adopted its Helios rack design. Helios contains 72 GPUs much like the DGX Vera Rubin NVL72. It’s based on AMD’s latest Instinct MI450 graphics card architecture, Epyc CPUs and Pensando data processing units, which are the chipmaker’s answer to the BlueField-4.
